function: BS precoder and STAR-RIS transmission/reflection phase design maximizing sum secrecy rate under CSI errors, learned by a two-agent (T-zone, R-zone) MA-PPO framework (p. 4, 10).
system: Downlink: BS with N=6 antennas, STAR-RIS with M=16 elements (energy splitting; phase-coupled variant also), K=6 single-antenna users, single-antenna eavesdroppers in each zone; 3.5 GHz (p. 4, 13).
method: Reinforcement learning: MA-PPO with two actor-critic agents (T-zone, R-zone) and a centralized memory buffer; single-agent PPO and DDPG also implemented; two hidden layers of 256 neurons (p. 10-13).
data_channel: Custom simulator: 3GPP-UMi reference path loss at 3.5 GHz (40 dB) with Rayleigh small-scale fading; norm-bounded CSI error of -15 dB; 100 channel realizations (p. 13).
test_conditions: Training with 2000 episodes of 500 steps; performance swept over transmit power, antennas, RIS elements, distance, Rmin, direct links; averaged over 100 channel realizations (p. 13-16).
baselines: Non-learned: conventional robust optimization (S-procedure, AO), passive RIS, random RIS, no RIS, perfect-CSI bound. Learned: single-agent PPO and DDPG (p. 13-14).
metrics: Sum secrecy rate in bits/s/Hz versus power, antennas, RIS elements, distance, Rmin; reward convergence over episodes (p. 14-16).
complexity: Complexity orders for robust optimization, proposed MA-PPO, PPO and DDPG in Table II (p. 13-14).
q1_support: p. 13: "The small-scale fading is assumed to be Rayleigh fading distribution"; only the 1 m reference path loss comes from the 3GPP-UMi model (ref. [57], TR 36.873, p. 18). Custom simulator, no 38.901, QuaDRiGa, DeepMIMO, or measured data.
q2_support: p. 13: "episodes E = 2000, steps ST = 500": agents train on the simulated setup and results are swept over power, antennas, RIS elements, distance, and Rmin (Figs. 5-11). The paper never states that a trained model is tested on a configuration, channel, or site unused in training, or after fine-tuning.
q3_support: p. 14: "The MA algorithm achieves a peak reward of 29.8 bits/s/Hz", above single-agent PPO (27.9) and DDPG (25.2); p. 15: "the proposed MA algorithm and conventional robust design achieve substantial secrecy sum rates of 31.33 and 20.6", with passive-RIS, random-RIS, and no-RIS also compared (p. 14).
q4_support: p. 13: "we examine the computational complexities associated with the robust optimization problem, MA-DRL-based algorithm, as well as those of the PPO, and DDPG, presented in Table II"; Table II (p. 14) lists O(.) expressions for the proposed MA algorithm.
q5_support: p. 13: "All the considered channels are assumed to include large-scale and small-scale fading": simulated channels. No code or data link, and no public dataset, appears in the 18 pages.
notes: PDF page 1 holds the title 'Robust and Secure Multi-User STAR-RIS-Aided Communications: Optimization Versus Machine Learning' and DOI 10.1109/TCOMM.2025.3541092. Included because the proposed MA-PPO learns the BS precoder and STAR-RIS coefficients (area 3); the classical robust solution (S-procedure, AO) is also in the paper but is not counted as learning. q3 rests on single-agent PPO and DDPG, standard algorithms applied to the same problem and compared on sum secrecy rate; the non-learned comparators are the conventional robust design and the passive, random, and no-RIS schemes. q1: only the reference path loss is taken from 3GPP, with Rayleigh fading.
